title: Mechanical power balance under adopted wall laws

items.title: Adopted Navier friction law for a stationary wall
items.design_state: Step 1 local postulate complete; the current continuum and boundary-data inputs are both Step-1 ready.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded domain with $C^2$ boundary, fixed in an inertial Euclidean frame, and let $n$ be its outward unit normal. On $\partial\Omega$, let $u$ be the trace of a $C^1$ fluid-velocity field in metres per second and let $\sigma$ be the Cauchy-stress tensor in pascals, with traction on the fluid defined by $\sigma n$. For a vector $a$, define its tangential projection by $a_\tau:=a-(a\cdot n)n$. Adopt impermeability $u\cdot n=0$ and the linear friction wall law

$$ (\sigma n)_\tau=-\beta u_\tau,$$

where $\beta\ge0$ is a constant with units pascal-seconds per metre. In the incompressible Newtonian branch, write the constant shear-viscosity coefficient as $\eta=\mu>0$ in pascal-seconds. For $\beta>0$, define the corresponding finite slip-length parameter by $\ell_s:=\eta/\beta$ metres; equivalently, $\beta=\eta/\ell_s$. The endpoint $\beta=0$ is zero tangential traction and has no finite $\ell_s$. This is a selected wall model, not a consequence of interior balance equations, a measured value of $\beta$, or a claim that any material or wall universally obeys it.

references.title: Gui-Qiang Chen and Zhongmin Qian, A Study of the Navier-Stokes Equations with the Kinematic and Navier Boundary Conditions
references.locator: arXiv:0901.0147v1, §1 equations (1.1), (1.3)–(1.4), and §2 equation (2.5) / Proposition 2.1, PDF pp. 1–5. The paper uses slip length ζ>0 and density-normalized viscosity; with σ=−pI+2ηD the friction coefficient here is β=η/ζ.

items.physical_scope: An adopted smooth stationary impermeable wall law for the incompressible Newtonian branch; no universality, measured coefficient, roughness derivation, or moving-wall slip law is asserted.

items.physical_scope: Smooth positive-density constant-density incompressible Newtonian material regions under the adopted integral momentum balance. It derives the local forced momentum equation by transport and localization; it asserts no solution existence or empirical validity.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval in seconds and let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open reference region. Let $\chi\in C^2(I\times B;\mathbb R^3)$ be a material motion whose maps $\chi_t$ are orientation-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphisms onto their open images, and define the Eulerian velocity by $u(t,\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\chi(t,a)$. Set $\Omega_t:=\chi_t(B)$ and $\mathcal O:=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\Omega_t\}$. Assume that $\partial_tu$ and all spatial derivatives of $u$ through order two are continuous on $\mathcal O$, that $p$ and its spatial first derivatives are continuous on $\mathcal O$, and that $b\in C^0(\mathcal O;\mathbb R^3)$; here $u$ is in metres per second, $p$ in pascals, and body acceleration $b$ in metres per second squared. In the selected constant-density incompressible Newtonian branch, let the current density be the constant $\rho>0$ kilograms per cubic metre, let $\operatorname{div}u=0$, let the coefficient $\mu$ of the adopted Newtonian closure be constant and denote its value by $\eta>0$ pascal-seconds. Put

$$D(u):=\frac{\nabla u+(\nabla u)^{\mathsf T}}2,\qquad \sigma:=-pI_3+2\eta D(u),\qquad (\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i:=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}.$$

Assume the adopted material linear-momentum balance holds for every nonempty bounded open $V\Subset B$ with $C^1$ boundary, meaning that near each boundary point, after a rigid coordinate change, the boundary is the graph of a $C^1$ function and $V$ lies on one side:

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho u\,dx=\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho b\,dx+\int_{\partial\chi_t(V)}\sigma n\,dS,$$

where $n$ is the outward normal and $dx,dS$ are Euclidean volume and area measures. Then throughout each $\Omega_t$ the corresponding local equation is

$$\rho\bigl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u\bigr)=\operatorname{div}\sigma+\rho b.$$

This is a conditional local form of the adopted balance for the stated smooth material motion and model branch; it makes no existence or empirical-applicability claim.

items.title: Mechanical power balance under adopted wall laws
items.design_state: Step 1 proof complete; the current smooth-wall uniqueness carrier, complete integrating-factor proof and readiness record match the bounded stationary use.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, meaning every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $T>0$ seconds. The spatial domain is either (B) a bounded connected nonempty open $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ with $C^2$ boundary, or (P) a periodic channel $\Omega_{L_x,h,L_z}:=(\mathbb R/L_x\mathbb Z)\times(0,h)\times(\mathbb R/L_z\mathbb Z)$ with $L_x,L_z,h>0$ metres. In (P), fields are periodic in the first and third coordinates on the Euclidean covering space, and the only physical wall boundary is $\Gamma=(\mathbb R/L_x\mathbb Z)\times\{0,h\}\times(\mathbb R/L_z\mathbb Z)$; identified periodic faces are not walls. In (B), set $\Gamma:=\partial\Omega$. In either case let $n$ be the outward unit normal on $\Gamma$, let $dx$ be Euclidean volume measure (or its periodic-cell quotient measure), and let $dS$ be the induced area measure on $\Gamma$. Let the constant mass density be $\rho>0$ kilograms per cubic metre, and let the coefficient $\mu$ of the adopted Newtonian closure be constant and denote its value by $\eta>0$ pascal-seconds; let the body-acceleration field be $b\in C([0,T]\times\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ in metres per second squared, the velocity be $u\in C^1([0,T];C^2(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$ in metres per second, and the pressure be $p\in C([0,T];C^1(\overline\Omega))$ in pascals. Define $D(u)_{ij}:=(\partial_{x_j}u_i+\partial_{x_i}u_j)/2$, $\sigma:=-pI+2\eta D(u)$, and rowwise $(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i:=\sum_j\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}$. For matrices $A,B\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ define the Frobenius contraction $A:B:=\sum_{i,j=1}^3A_{ij}B_{ij}$ and the squared norm $|D(u)|^2:=D(u):D(u)=\sum_{i,j=1}^3D(u)_{ij}^2$. In the proof, $D$ abbreviates $D(u)$. Put $I=(0,T)$. In case (B), put $B=\Omega$ and assume $\chi\in C^2(I\times B;\mathbb R^3)$, with each $\chi_t:B\to B$ an orientation-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphism, and $u(t,\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\chi(t,a)$. In case (P), put $\widetilde\Omega=\mathbb R\times(0,h)\times\mathbb R$ and $\Lambda=\{(mL_x,0,nL_z):m,n\in\mathbb Z\}$; denote periodic lifts of $u,b,\sigma$ by $\widetilde u,\widetilde b,\widetilde\sigma$. Assume $\widetilde\chi\in C^2(I\times\widetilde\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$, with each $\widetilde\chi_t:\widetilde\Omega\to\widetilde\Omega$ an orientation-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphism satisfying $\widetilde\chi(t,a+\lambda)=\widetilde\chi(t,a)+\lambda$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$, and $\widetilde u(t,\widetilde\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\widetilde\chi(t,a)$. For the material balance, write $(B,\chi,u^\sharp,b^\sharp,\sigma^\sharp)=(\Omega,\chi,u,b,\sigma)$ in case (B), and $(B,\chi,u^\sharp,b^\sharp,\sigma^\sharp)=(\widetilde\Omega,\widetilde\chi,\widetilde u,\widetilde b,\widetilde\sigma)$ in case (P). Here $\nu$ denotes the outward unit normal of $\chi_t(V)$; in case (P), the material-region integrals are on the Euclidean covering space. For every $t\in I$ and every nonempty bounded open $V\Subset B$ with $C^1$ boundary, assume the adopted material linear-momentum balance

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho u^\sharp\,dx=\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho b^\sharp\,dx+\int_{\partial\chi_t(V)}\sigma^\sharp\nu\,dS,$$

Assume incompressibility as a model constraint, $\operatorname{div}u=0$ throughout the fluid domain (and $\operatorname{div}\widetilde u=0$ on its lift in case (P)). At every time impose one of the following wall laws: (N) no-slip, $u=g$ on $\Gamma$ for a prescribed tangential wall-velocity field $g\in C^1([0,T];C^2(\Gamma;\mathbb R^3))$ in metres per second with $g\cdot n=0$; or (S) stationary Navier friction on branch (B) only, $u\cdot n=0$ and $(\sigma n)_\tau=-\beta u_\tau$ on $\Gamma$, where $a_\tau:=a-(a\cdot n)n$ and $\beta\ge0$ is the adopted constant wall coefficient in pascal-seconds per metre. Then the local momentum equation

$$\rho\bigl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u\bigr)=\operatorname{div}\sigma+\rho b$$

holds on the fluid domain by the local momentum result from the adopted material balance; incompressibility is the separate model constraint stated above, not a conclusion of that result. Let $K(t):=\int_\Omega \rho|u(t,x)|^2/2\,dx$. Then for every $t\in(0,T)$ in case (N),

$$\frac{dK}{dt}=\int_\Omega \rho b\cdot u\,dx-2\eta\int_\Omega |D(u)|^2\,dx+\int_{\Gamma}g\cdot\sigma n\,dS,$$

and for every $t\in(0,T)$ in case (S),

$$\frac{dK}{dt}=\int_\Omega \rho b\cdot u\,dx-2\eta\int_\Omega |D(u)|^2\,dx-\beta\int_{\Gamma}|u_\tau|^2\,dS.$$

Every term has units of watts. In branch (B) only, in either stationary homogeneous case, (N) with $g=0$ or (S) with a fixed $\beta$, there is at most one velocity field $u$ in this smooth class for a given body force and initial velocity. No pressure uniqueness is asserted. These are deductions conditional on the stated model and wall assumptions; no solution-existence or empirical-applicability claim is made.

items.physical_scope: Smooth incompressible Newtonian solutions of constant positive density and viscosity on a fixed bounded C2 domain, or on the stated periodic channel with no-slip physical walls. The adopted stationary Navier friction law is used only on the bounded-domain branch. It gives conditional mechanical power identities and stationary bounded-domain smooth uniqueness only; no existence or universal wall-law applicability is asserted.

items.title: Linear acoustic model prediction
items.design_state: Step 1 conditional proof complete; the current barotropic definition and global tangent-system theorem match and both are Step-1 ready.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval measured in seconds with $0\in I$, let $L=1\,\mathrm m$, and let $\Omega_L:=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi L\mathbb Z)^3$ be a spatial periodic cell with coordinates in metres and volume measure $dx$ induced from a fundamental cell. Let $p:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a $C^1$ barotropic pressure law in pascals, let $\rho_*>0$ be a constant reference density in kilograms per cubic metre, and assume $p'(\rho_*)>0$ in square metres per second squared. The adopted no-force barotropic Euler model is

$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0,\qquad \rho\bigl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u\bigr)+\nabla p(\rho)=0,$$

for periodic fields $\rho\in C^2(I\times\Omega_L;(0,\infty))$ and $u\in C^2(I\times\Omega_L;\mathbb R^3)$, where density is in kilograms per cubic metre and velocity is in metres per second. Here $C^\infty$ means that coordinate derivatives of every finite order are continuous, with spatial fields periodic on $\Omega_L$. The uniform state $(\rho,u)=(\rho_*,0)$ is an equilibrium. For perturbations $z\in C^\infty(I\times\Omega_L;\mathbb R)$ and $v\in C^\infty(I\times\Omega_L;\mathbb R^3)$, define the tangent model as the pointwise first variation at the dimensionless parameter $\epsilon=0$ of this equation operator on $\rho_\epsilon=\rho_*+\epsilon z$ and $u_\epsilon=\epsilon v$; on each compact time interval these perturbed densities remain positive for sufficiently small $|\epsilon|$. For arbitrary initial data $z_0\in C^\infty(\Omega_L;\mathbb R)$ and $v_0\in C^\infty(\Omega_L;\mathbb R^3)$, where these fields have continuous spatial derivatives of every finite order and are periodic, that tangent model is

$$\partial_t z+\rho_*\operatorname{div}v=0,\qquad \partial_t v+\frac{c_*^2}{\rho_*}\nabla z=0,\qquad (z,v)|_{t=0}=(z_0,v_0),\qquad c_*:=\sqrt{p'(\rho_*)}>0.$$

Here $z$ is a density perturbation in kilograms per cubic metre, $v$ is a velocity perturbation in metres per second, and $c_*$ is the model sound speed in metres per second. For every such initial pair, this linear tangent system has a unique real $C^\infty$ solution $(z,v):\mathbb R\times\Omega_L\to\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$. Its acoustic energy

$$E_{\mathrm{ac}}(t):=\frac12\int_{\Omega_L}\left(\rho_*|v|^2+\frac{c_*^2}{\rho_*}z^2\right)\,dx$$

is constant in joules. For a scalar or vector field $f$, take vector coefficients componentwise; for a wavevector $\kappa\in L^{-1}\mathbb Z^3$, use the Fourier character $e_\kappa(x)=e^{i\kappa\cdot x}$ and normalized coefficient $\widehat f(\kappa,t)=((2\pi L)^3)^{-1}\int_{\Omega_L}f(t,x)e^{-i\kappa\cdot x}\,dx$, with the integral taken over a fundamental cell. For $\kappa\ne0$, the longitudinal velocity coefficient is $\widehat v_\parallel=(\kappa\cdot\widehat v)|\kappa|^{-2}\kappa$ and the transverse coefficient is $\widehat v_\perp=\widehat v-\widehat v_\parallel$. A nonzero longitudinal normal mode is a nonzero Fourier solution with $\widehat v_\perp=0$ and time dependence $e^{-i\omega t}$; its angular frequency $\omega$ in inverse seconds satisfies $\omega^2=c_*^2|\kappa|^2$. The transverse coefficient at each $\kappa\ne0$, and the mean coefficients $\widehat z(0,t),\widehat v(0,t)$ at $\kappa=0$, are constant in time. These are exact deductions for the specified linear tangent model, not a finite-amplitude approximation theorem, an observation, or a claim that an actual fluid follows the model.

references.title: David Tong, Fluid Mechanics, Chapter 3
references.locator: §4.4.4, printed pp. 150–152 (PDF pp. 39–42): linearized Euler and mass equations, adiabatic sound speed, wave equation and Fourier-mode dispersion.

items.title: Adopted Poiseuille and Couette channel predictions
items.design_state: Step 1 worked example complete; its wall-power supplier and all current prerequisites are present, match and are ready.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, meaning every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $L_x,L_z,h>0$ be lengths in metres and let $\Omega=(\mathbb R/L_x\mathbb Z)\times(0,h)\times(\mathbb R/L_z\mathbb Z)$ have periodic streamwise coordinate $x$ and spanwise coordinate $z$, with stationary walls $y=0,h$; all three coordinates are measured in metres. Let $\rho>0$ be constant density in kilograms per cubic metre, $\eta>0$ constant dynamic viscosity in pascal-seconds, and $p_0$ a constant pressure in pascals. Use the incompressible Newtonian model $\rho(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u)=\operatorname{div}\sigma+\rho b$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, $\sigma=-pI+2\eta D(u)$, where $D(u)_{ij}=(\partial_j u_i+\partial_i u_j)/2$ and divergence is rowwise. For matrices $A,B\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ define the Frobenius contraction $A:B:=\sum_{i,j=1}^3A_{ij}B_{ij}$ and the squared norm $|D(u)|^2:=D(u):D(u)=\sum_{i,j=1}^3D(u)_{ij}^2$. In the verification, $D$ abbreviates $D(u)$. In the Poiseuille case let $G>0$ be a pressure-gradient scale in pascals per metre, set the body acceleration $b=(G/\rho,0,0)$ in metres per second squared and $p=p_0$, and define

$$u_P(x,y,z)=\left(\frac{G\,y(h-y)}{2\eta},0,0\right).$$

In the Couette case let $V\in\mathbb R$ be a tangential wall speed in metres per second, set $b=0$, $p=p_0$, and define

$$u_C(x,y,z)=\left(\frac{Vy}{h},0,0\right),$$

with no-slip wall velocity $g=0$ at $y=0$ and $g=(V,0,0)$ at $y=h$. Both fields are exact steady smooth solutions with impermeable no-slip walls. Their volumetric fluxes per unit span are $Q_P=Gh^3/(12\eta)$ and $Q_C=Vh/2$, each in square metres per second, and their vorticities $\omega:=\nabla\times u$ in inverse seconds are $\omega_P=(0,0,-G(h-2y)/(2\eta))$ and $\omega_C=(0,0,-V/h)$. In the Poiseuille case the body-force power per unit wall area equals viscous dissipation and stationary walls do no work. In the Couette case the moving top wall supplies power equal to viscous dissipation. A periodic pressure cannot contain the nonperiodic term $-Gx$; the stated constant pressure and body acceleration are the periodic-cell formulation. These are conditional predictions of the adopted equations, not observations or claims about all fluids.

references.title: David Tong, Fluid Mechanics, Chapter 2
references.locator: §§3.2.2–3.2.3, printed pp. 65–68 (PDF pp. 10–14): exact Couette and planar Poiseuille profiles with no-slip walls.

references.title: Joseph M. Powers, Lecture Notes on Intermediate Fluid Mechanics
references.locator: §5.4.1, printed pp. 173–175: Couette setup, no-slip convention, and shear-stress/strain-rate relation.

items.physical_scope: Exact steady profiles in the stated periodic incompressible Newtonian channel model with no-slip walls; the Poiseuille pressure-drop notation is replaced by a constant body acceleration on the periodic cell. No measured flow or claim about a named material is included.
